</span></div></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">
<p id="S4.T3.6" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left ltx_figure_panel"><math id="S4.T3.m44" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\dagger" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo mathsize="0.800em">†</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\dagger</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.T3.6.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;"> ProfilingDiT and TaylorSeer can only generate up to 17 frames at 544p<math id="S4.T3.m45" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math>860p resolution on a single A800 GPU, and run OOM at 480p<math id="S4.T3.m46" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math>640p with 45 frames.</span></p></div></div>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.3 </span>Text-to-Video Generation</h3>

<div id="S4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Quantitative Results.</span>
We extend our evaluation to text-to-video generation on HunyuanVideo, testing two resolution settings as shown in <a href="#S4.T3" title="In 4.2 Text-to-Image Generation ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Predict to Skip: Linear Multistep Feature Forecasting for Efficient Diffusion Transformers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>. At 544p<math id="S4.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math>860p with 17 frames, PrediT achieves <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="3.28\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3.28</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.28\times</annotation></semantics></math> speedup while maintaining the highest VBench score and best visual metrics. Compared to other methods, PAB and TeaCache provide limited speedups with 50 sampling steps. Prediction-based methods face challenges in video generation; for example, TaylorSeer achieves comparable speedup but with degraded visual quality, indicating accumulated prediction errors across video frames. AB-Cache shows better quality retention but PrediT still outperforms it in both acceleration and visual fidelity. At 480p<math id="S4.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math>640p with 45 frames, the computational challenge increases, yet PrediT maintains consistent acceleration with the best VBench score. Notably, ProfilingDiT and TaylorSeer encounter out-of-memory (OOM) errors at this setting, highlighting the memory efficiency of our approach. Detailed memory analysis is provided in <a href="#A7" title="Appendix G Memory Usage Analysis ‣ Predict to Skip: Linear Multistep Feature Forecasting for Efficient Diffusion Transformers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">G</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F6" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">
<figure id="S4.F6.sf1" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18093v1/acceleration_544x960.svg" id="S4.F6.sf1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/332;" width="476" height="332"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F6.sf1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">(a)</span> </span><span id="S4.F6.sf1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">544P</span></figcaption>
</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">
<figure id="S4.F6.sf2" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18093v1/acceleration_720x1280.svg" id="S4.F6.sf2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/332;" width="476" height="332"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F6.sf2.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">(b)</span> </span><span id="S4.F6.sf2.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">720P</span></figcaption>
</figure></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F6.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 6</span>: </span><span id="S4.F6.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Latency comparison between the original method and PrediT on HunyuanVideo at 544P and 720P resolutions across different frame counts.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Scaling Analysis.</span>
<a href="#S4.F6" title="In 4.3 Text-to-Video Generation ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Predict to Skip: Linear Multistep Feature Forecasting for Efficient Diffusion Transformers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> illustrates the latency scaling behavior across different frame counts at 544P and 720P resolutions. The original method exhibits near-linear latency growth with increasing frames, becoming prohibitive for longer video generation. PrediT consistently reduces latency across all configurations, with the acceleration ratio remaining stable as frame count increases. This demonstrates that our dynamic step modulation adapts effectively to the temporal structure of video diffusion, maintaining efficient inference regardless of video length.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Visual Comparison.</span>
<a href="#S4.F7" title="In 4.3 Text-to-Video Generation ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Predict to Skip: Linear Multistep Feature Forecasting for Efficient Diffusion Transformers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> presents visual comparisons on HunyuanVideo. Other acceleration methods suffer from noticeable quality degradation, including blurriness and loss of fine details in both spatial and temporal dimensions. PrediT preserves the visual quality of the original model, with sharp details and consistent motion across frames, validating the effectiveness of our predictor-corrector scheme.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F7" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18093v1/hy.png" id="S4.F7.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/210;" width="476" height="210" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F7.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 7</span>: </span><span id="S4.F7.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Visual quality comparison of different acceleration methods on HunyuanVideo. Other acceleration methods suffer from blurriness or loss of details, while PrediT maintains comparable visual quality with higher acceleration.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.4 </span>Class-to-Image Generation</h3>

<div id="S4.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Quantitative Results.</span>
In <a href="#S4.T4" title="In 4.4 Class-to-Image Generation ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Predict to Skip: Linear Multistep Feature Forecasting for Efficient Diffusion Transformers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>, we evaluate PrediT on DiT-XL/2 for class-conditional ImageNet generation, comparing with existing acceleration methods under both 50-step and 70-step DDIM sampling. Notably, Learning-to-Cache (L2C) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib55" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ma et al., 2024a</a>)</cite> learns to conduct caching in a dynamic manner for diffusion transformers, which is not training-free. At 50 steps, PrediT achieves <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="2.12\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.12</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.12\times</annotation></semantics></math> speedup while improving FID from 2.28 to 2.24, demonstrating that our method can simultaneously accelerate inference and enhance generation quality. This improvement stems from the reduced discretization error of our higher-order prediction scheme. In comparison, FORA achieves <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="2.03\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.03</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.03\times</annotation></semantics></math> speedup but degrades FID to 3.52, and L2C provides only <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.25\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.25</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.25\times</annotation></semantics></math> acceleration. At 70 steps, PrediT maintains consistent performance with <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="2.48\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.48</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.48\times</annotation></semantics></math> speedup and FID of 2.24. Notably, TaylorSeer exhibits severe quality collapse at 70 steps with FID degrading to 10.12, indicating numerical instability in its Taylor series extrapolation over longer sampling trajectories. PrediT avoids this issue through the stability properties of Adams methods and adaptive corrector activation.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Quality-Speedup Trade-off.</span>
<a href="#S4.F8" title="In 4.4 Class-to-Image Generation ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Predict to Skip: Linear Multistep Feature Forecasting for Efficient Diffusion Transformers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> visualizes the quality-speedup trade-off between DDIM and PrediT with different predictor orders. Higher-order predictors achieve better FID and IS at the cost of slightly reduced speedup. Notably, PrediT with <math id="S4.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}=4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}=4</annotation></semantics></math> surpasses the DDIM baseline in both FID and IS while still providing acceleration, demonstrating that our method can improve quality while accelerating inference. Suggesting that users choose the parameters flexibly.
Additional ablation studies with various hyperparameter configurations are provided in <a href="#A8" title="Appendix H Supplementary Results for Ablation Studies ‣ Predict to Skip: Linear Multistep Feature Forecasting for Efficient Diffusion Transformers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">H</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.T4" class="ltx_table">

<td id="S4.T4.5.1.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_r ltx_border_tt"><span id="S4.T4.5.1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Steps</span></td>
<td id="S4.T4.5.1.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt"><span id="S4.T4.5.1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Latency(s) <math id="S4.T4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\downarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\downarrow</annotation></semantics></math></span></td>

</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this paper, we presented PrediT, a training-free acceleration framework for DiTs that formulates feature prediction as a linear multistep problem. Observing that model outputs evolve smoothly along the diffusion trajectory, we moved beyond naive feature reuse to principled prediction. Our framework employs the Adams-Bashforth predictor to extrapolate future model outputs from historical information, and an Adams-Moulton corrector that activates in high-dynamics regions to prevent error accumulation. The dynamic step modulation mechanism adaptively adjusts the prediction horizon based on the relative feature change rate, enabling aggressive skipping in smooth regions while maintaining accuracy in high-dynamics regions. Experiments across DiT-based models demonstrate the effectiveness of PrediT. Future work includes extending our framework to emerging architectures such as Mixture-of-Experts DiT models and exploring applications in interactive generation scenarios.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="Sx1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section">Impact Statements</h2>

<div id="Sx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This paper presents work whose goal is to advance the field of machine learning, particularly in efficient inference for generative models. The proposed PrediT framework has several positive societal implications:</p>
<ul id="Sx1.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="Sx1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Sx1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Environmental Efficiency:</span> By reducing model inference latency while maintaining generation quality, our method directly lowers the energy consumption and carbon footprint of running large-scale diffusion models for image and video generation.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Sx1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Sx1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx1.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Democratization of Access:</span> Our method introduces minimal memory overhead, enabling high-resolution video generation on a consumer-grade GPU without out-of-memory errors. This broadens access to advanced generative tools for researchers and creators with limited computational resources.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>

<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Adams Method Coefficients</h2>

<section id="A1.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.1 </span>Derivation of Second-Order Adams-Bashforth (AB2)</h3>

<div id="A1.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The Adams-Bashforth method approximates the integral <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\int_{t_{n}}^{t_{n+1}}f(x(s),s)\,ds" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo>∫</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msubsup><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_{t_{n}}^{t_{n+1}}f(x(s),s)\,ds</annotation></semantics></math> by constructing a Lagrange interpolating polynomial through historical function values. For the second-order case (AB2), we use two points <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(t_{n},f_{n})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(t_{n},f_{n})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(t_{n-1},f_{n-1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(t_{n-1},f_{n-1})</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The Lagrange interpolating polynomial is:</p>
<table id="A1.E11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P(s)=f_{n}\cdot\frac{s-t_{n-1}}{t_{n}-t_{n-1}}+f_{n-1}\cdot\frac{s-t_{n}}{t_{n-1}-t_{n}}=f_{n}\cdot\frac{s-t_{n-1}}{h}-f_{n-1}\cdot\frac{s-t_{n}}{h}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mi>h</mi></mfrac></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow><mi>h</mi></mfrac></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P(s)=f_{n}\cdot\frac{s-t_{n-1}}{t_{n}-t_{n-1}}+f_{n-1}\cdot\frac{s-t_{n}}{t_{n-1}-t_{n}}=f_{n}\cdot\frac{s-t_{n-1}}{h}-f_{n-1}\cdot\frac{s-t_{n}}{h},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(11)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h=\Delta t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h=\Delta t</annotation></semantics></math> is the uniform step size. Integrating from <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{n}</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{n+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{n+1}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="A1.EGx1" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A1.E12"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\int_{t_{n}}^{t_{n+1}}P(s)\,ds" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><msubsup><mo>∫</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msubsup></mstyle><mrow><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\int_{t_{n}}^{t_{n+1}}P(s)\,ds</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E12.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\frac{f_{n}}{h}\int_{t_{n}}^{t_{n+1}}(s-t_{n-1})\,ds-\frac{f_{n-1}}{h}\int_{t_{n}}^{t_{n+1}}(s-t_{n})\,ds" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mi>h</mi></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><msubsup><mo>∫</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msubsup></mstyle><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mi>h</mi></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><msubsup><mo>∫</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msubsup></mstyle><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\frac{f_{n}}{h}\int_{t_{n}}^{t_{n+1}}(s-t_{n-1})\,ds-\frac{f_{n-1}}{h}\int_{t_{n}}^{t_{n+1}}(s-t_{n})\,ds</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(12)</span></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="A1.E13"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\frac{f_{n}}{h}\left[\frac{(s-t_{n-1})^{2}}{2}\right]_{t_{n}}^{t_{n+1}}-\frac{f_{n-1}}{h}\left[\frac{(s-t_{n})^{2}}{2}\right]_{t_{n}}^{t_{n+1}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mi>h</mi></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo>[</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo>]</mo></mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msubsup></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mi>h</mi></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo>[</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo>]</mo></mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\frac{f_{n}}{h}\left[\frac{(s-t_{n-1})^{2}}{2}\right]_{t_{n}}^{t_{n+1}}-\frac{f_{n-1}}{h}\left[\frac{(s-t_{n})^{2}}{2}\right]_{t_{n}}^{t_{n+1}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(13)</span></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="A1.E14"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\frac{f_{n}}{h}\cdot\frac{(2h)^{2}-h^{2}}{2}-\frac{f_{n-1}}{h}\cdot\frac{h^{2}}{2}=\frac{3h}{2}f_{n}-\frac{h}{2}f_{n-1}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mi>h</mi></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mi>h</mi></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><msup><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\frac{f_{n}}{h}\cdot\frac{(2h)^{2}-h^{2}}{2}-\frac{f_{n-1}}{h}\cdot\frac{h^{2}}{2}=\frac{3h}{2}f_{n}-\frac{h}{2}f_{n-1}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(14)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS1.p2.3" class="ltx_p">Thus, the AB2 formula is:</p>
<table id="A1.E15" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{n+1}=x_{n}+\frac{h}{2}(3f_{n}-f_{n-1})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{n+1}=x_{n}+\frac{h}{2}(3f_{n}-f_{n-1}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(15)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS1.p2.4" class="ltx_p">with coefficients <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta_{0}=\frac{3}{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta_{0}=\frac{3}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta_{1}=-\frac{1}{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta_{1}=-\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>

</section>
<section id="A1.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.2 </span>Derivation of Second-Order Adams-Moulton (AM2)</h3>

<div id="A1.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The Adams-Moulton method includes the future value <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{n+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{n+1}</annotation></semantics></math> in the interpolation, making it implicit. For the second-order case (AM2), we construct a polynomial through three points <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(t_{n+1},f_{n+1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(t_{n+1},f_{n+1})</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(t_{n},f_{n})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(t_{n},f_{n})</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(t_{n-1},f_{n-1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(t_{n-1},f_{n-1})</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="A1.E16" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E16.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P(s)=f_{n+1}L_{-1}(s)+f_{n}L_{0}(s)+f_{n-1}L_{1}(s)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P(s)=f_{n+1}L_{-1}(s)+f_{n}L_{0}(s)+f_{n-1}L_{1}(s),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(16)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{j}(s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{j}(s)</annotation></semantics></math> are the Lagrange basis polynomials. After computing the integrals:</p>
<table id="A1.EGx2" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A1.E17"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\int_{t_{n}}^{t_{n+1}}L_{-1}(s)\,ds" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><msubsup><mo>∫</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msubsup></mstyle><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\int_{t_{n}}^{t_{n+1}}L_{-1}(s)\,ds</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E17.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\frac{5h}{12},\quad\int_{t_{n}}^{t_{n+1}}L_{0}(s)\,ds=\frac{8h}{12},\quad\int_{t_{n}}^{t_{n+1}}L_{1}(s)\,ds=-\frac{h}{12}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><mn>12</mn></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><msubsup><mo>∫</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msubsup></mstyle><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><mn>12</mn></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><msubsup><mo>∫</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msubsup></mstyle><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mi>h</mi><mn>12</mn></mfrac></mstyle></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\frac{5h}{12},\quad\int_{t_{n}}^{t_{n+1}}L_{0}(s)\,ds=\frac{8h}{12},\quad\int_{t_{n}}^{t_{n+1}}L_{1}(s)\,ds=-\frac{h}{12}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(17)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS2.p1.3" class="ltx_p">Thus, the AM2 formula is:</p>
<table id="A1.E18" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E18.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{n+1}=x_{n}+\frac{h}{12}(5f_{n+1}+8f_{n}-f_{n-1})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>h</mi><mn>12</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{n+1}=x_{n}+\frac{h}{12}(5f_{n+1}+8f_{n}-f_{n-1}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(18)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS2.p1.4" class="ltx_p">with coefficients <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma_{-1}=\frac{5}{12}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>γ</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>12</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma_{-1}=\frac{5}{12}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma_{0}=\frac{8}{12}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>γ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>8</mn><mn>12</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma_{0}=\frac{8}{12}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma_{1}=-\frac{1}{12}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>12</mn></mfrac></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma_{1}=-\frac{1}{12}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.3 </span>Higher-Order Coefficients</h3>

<div id="A1.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Following the same derivation procedure, we obtain coefficients for higher-order methods. <a href="#A1.T5" title="In A.3 Higher-Order Coefficients ‣ Appendix A Adams Method Coefficients ‣ Predict to Skip: Linear Multistep Feature Forecasting for Efficient Diffusion Transformers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> and <a href="#A1.T6" title="In A.3 Higher-Order Coefficients ‣ Appendix A Adams Method Coefficients ‣ Predict to Skip: Linear Multistep Feature Forecasting for Efficient Diffusion Transformers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> summarize the coefficients and local truncation errors (LTE) for orders 1–4.</p>
</div>

<div id="A1.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Note that AM of the same order has a smaller LTE coefficient than AB, providing improved accuracy at the cost of requiring <math id="A1.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{n+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{n+1}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>

</section>
<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>Error Analysis</h2>

<section id="A2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.1 </span>Discretization Error</h3>

<div id="A2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For an ODE <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\dot{x}=f(x,t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>˙</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\dot{x}=f(x,t)</annotation></semantics></math> with exact solution <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(t)</annotation></semantics></math>, the local truncation error (LTE) of a numerical method measures the error introduced in a single step assuming exact previous values.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition B.1</span></span><span id="A2.Thmtheorem1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(AB Local Truncation Error)<span id="A2.Thmtheorem1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">The Adams-Bashforth method of order <math id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> has LTE:</span></p>
<table id="A2.E19" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E19.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{n}^{AB}=C_{k}h^{k+1}f^{(k)}(\xi)+\mathcal{O}(h^{k+2})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><mi>n</mi><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ξ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{n}^{AB}=C_{k}h^{k+1}f^{(k)}(\xi)+\mathcal{O}(h^{k+2}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(19)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">where <math id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> is a constant depending on <math id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\xi\in[t_{n},t_{n+1}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ξ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\xi\in[t_{n},t_{n+1}]</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The global error after <math id="A2.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> steps is bounded by:</p>
<table id="A2.E20" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E20.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|x_{N}-x(t_{N})\|\leq\frac{e^{LT}-1}{L}\max_{n}\|\tau_{n}\|=\mathcal{O}(h^{k})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>L</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><munder><mi>max</mi><mi>n</mi></munder><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mi>k</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|x_{N}-x(t_{N})\|\leq\frac{e^{LT}-1}{L}\max_{n}\|\tau_{n}\|=\mathcal{O}(h^{k}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(20)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A2.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math> is the Lipschitz constant of <math id="A2.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> is the total integration time.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.2 </span>Prediction Error During Skips</h3>

<div id="A2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">When skipping model calls, we use AB to predict <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{n+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{n+1}</annotation></semantics></math> from history:</p>
<table id="A2.E21" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E21.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{f}_{n+1}=\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\alpha_{j}f_{n-j}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></munderover><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{f}_{n+1}=\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\alpha_{j}f_{n-j},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(21)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> are extrapolation coefficients. The prediction error is:</p>
<table id="A2.E22" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E22.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon_{\text{pred}}=\|f_{n+1}-\hat{f}_{n+1}\|\approx\mathcal{O}(h^{k}\|f^{(k)}\|)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mtext>pred</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>h</mi><mi>k</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon_{\text{pred}}=\|f_{n+1}-\hat{f}_{n+1}\|\approx\mathcal{O}(h^{k}\|f^{(k)}\|).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(22)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">This error depends on the local curvature of the trajectory. Our dynamics metric <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{n}</annotation></semantics></math> approximates the first derivative, providing a proxy for curvature.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.3 </span>Error Accumulation and Mitigation</h3>

<div id="A2.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">When <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>J</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J</annotation></semantics></math> consecutive steps are skipped, errors accumulate:</p>
<table id="A2.E23" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E23.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon_{\text{acc}}(J)\approx\sum_{i=1}^{J}\epsilon_{\text{pred}}(i)\cdot(1+Lh)^{J-i}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mtext>acc</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>J</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">≈</mo><mrow><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>J</mi></munderover><mrow><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mtext>pred</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon_{\text{acc}}(J)\approx\sum_{i=1}^{J}\epsilon_{\text{pred}}(i)\cdot(1+Lh)^{J-i}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(23)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The exponential factor <math id="A2.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(1+Lh)^{J-i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1+Lh)^{J-i}</annotation></semantics></math> reflects error propagation through the ODE. Our framework mitigates this through:</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<ol id="A2.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="A2.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="A2.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Adaptive skip interval</span>: When <math id="A2.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{n}</annotation></semantics></math> is large, <math id="A2.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>J</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J</annotation></semantics></math> is automatically reduced via <a href="#S3.E10" title="In 3.2 PrediT Framework ‣ 3 Method ‣ Predict to Skip: Linear Multistep Feature Forecasting for Efficient Diffusion Transformers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Equation</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="A2.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">ABM correction</span>: When <math id="A2.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{n}\geq\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>≥</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{n}\geq\tau</annotation></semantics></math>, we invoke ABM which evaluates the true <math id="A2.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{n+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{n+1}</annotation></semantics></math>, resetting the prediction error to the discretization error of AM.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="A2.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Threshold-based switching</span>: The correction ratio <math id="A2.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> creates a buffer zone where ABM is used even for moderate dynamics.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition B.2</span></span><span id="A2.Thmtheorem2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Error Bound with Dynamic Step Modulation)<span id="A2.Thmtheorem2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.Thmtheorem2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Under the assumption that <math id="A2.Thmtheorem2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|f^{(k)}\|\leq M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|f^{(k)}\|\leq M</annotation></semantics></math> and with threshold <math id="A2.Thmtheorem2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> chosen such that <math id="A2.Thmtheorem2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{n}&lt;\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{n}&lt;\tau</annotation></semantics></math> implies <math id="A2.Thmtheorem2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|f^{\prime}\|\leq\tau\|f\|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|f^{\prime}\|\leq\tau\|f\|</annotation></semantics></math>, the accumulated error over a trajectory satisfies:</span></p>
<table id="A2.E24" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E24.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\epsilon_{\text{total}}\|\leq C_{1}h^{k}+C_{2}\tau J_{\max}+C_{3}N_{\text{ABM}}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">total</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mi>k</mi></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>J</mi><mi>max</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">ABM</mtext></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\epsilon_{\text{total}}\|\leq C_{1}h^{k}+C_{2}\tau J_{\max}+C_{3}N_{\text{ABM}},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(24)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.Thmtheorem2.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem2.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">where <math id="A2.Thmtheorem2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J_{\max}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>J</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J_{\max}</annotation></semantics></math> is the maximum allowed skip interval and <math id="A2.Thmtheorem2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{\text{ABM}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">ABM</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{\text{ABM}}</annotation></semantics></math> is the number of ABM corrections that reset the accumulated drift.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">This shows that the error is controlled by the interplay between the method order <math id="A2.SS3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>, the threshold <math id="A2.SS3.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>, and the frequency of corrections.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>

</div>

</div>
<div id="alg1.l6" class="ltx_listingline">

<div id="alg1.l7" class="ltx_listingline">
            
            
            <span id="alg1.l7.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">else</span>


</div>
<div id="alg1.l8" class="ltx_listingline">
            
            
             <math id="alg1.l8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{n}\leftarrow f_{\theta}(x,t_{n})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{n}\leftarrow f_{\theta}(x,t_{n})</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="alg1.l8.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">// Compute model output</span>

</div>
<div id="alg1.l9" class="ltx_listingline">
            
            
             <math id="alg1.l9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{n}\leftarrow\|f_{n}-f_{n-1}\|_{1}/(\|f_{n}\|_{1}+\epsilon)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{n}\leftarrow\|f_{n}-f_{n-1}\|_{1}/(\|f_{n}\|_{1}+\epsilon)</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="alg1.l9.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">// Dynamics metric</span>

</div>
<div id="alg1.l10" class="ltx_listingline">
            
            
             <span id="alg1.l10.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">if</span> <math id="alg1.l10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{n}\geq\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>≥</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{n}\geq\tau</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="alg1.l10.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">then</span>



</div>
<div id="alg1.l11" class="ltx_listingline">
            
            
              <math id="alg1.l11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\leftarrow\text{ABM}_{k}(x,\Delta t,f_{n},\mathcal{H},f_{\theta})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><msub><mtext>ABM</mtext><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\leftarrow\text{ABM}_{k}(x,\Delta t,f_{n},\mathcal{H},f_{\theta})</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="alg1.l11.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">// Corrected by ABM</span>

</div>
<div id="alg1.l12" class="ltx_listingline">
            
            
             <span id="alg1.l12.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">else</span> <span id="alg1.l12.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">if</span> <math id="alg1.l12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{n}\geq\tau\cdot r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{n}\geq\tau\cdot r</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="alg1.l12.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">then</span>



</div>
<div id="alg1.l13" class="ltx_listingline">
            
            
              <math id="alg1.l13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\leftarrow\text{ABM}_{k}(x,\Delta t,f_{n},\mathcal{H},f_{\theta})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><msub><mtext>ABM</mtext><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\leftarrow\text{ABM}_{k}(x,\Delta t,f_{n},\mathcal{H},f_{\theta})</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="alg1.l13.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J\leftarrow\text{ComputeSkip}(\delta_{n},\tau)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mtext>ComputeSkip</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J\leftarrow\text{ComputeSkip}(\delta_{n},\tau)</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="alg1.l13.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">// Corrected by ABM with dynamic step modulation</span>

</div>
<div id="alg1.l14" class="ltx_listingline">
            
            
             <span id="alg1.l14.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">else</span>


</div>
<div id="alg1.l15" class="ltx_listingline">
            
            
              <math id="alg1.l15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\leftarrow x+\text{AB}_{k}(\Delta t,[f_{n}]\cup\mathcal{H})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mtext>AB</mtext><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>∪</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\leftarrow x+\text{AB}_{k}(\Delta t,[f_{n}]\cup\mathcal{H})</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="alg1.l15.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J\leftarrow\text{ComputeSkip}(\delta_{n},\tau)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mtext>ComputeSkip</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J\leftarrow\text{ComputeSkip}(\delta_{n},\tau)</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="alg1.l15.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">// Predicted by AB with dynamic step modulation</span>

             <span id="alg1.l16.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">end</span> <span id="alg1.l16.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">if</span>
</div>
<div id="alg1.l17" class="ltx_listingline">
            
            
             Update <math id="alg1.l17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{H}\leftarrow[f_{n}]\cup\mathcal{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>∪</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{H}\leftarrow[f_{n}]\cup\mathcal{H}</annotation></semantics></math>

           <span id="alg1.l19.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">end</span> <span id="alg1.l19.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">for</span>

           <span id="alg1.l20.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">return</span> <math id="alg1.l20.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>
