<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Evaluation Metrics</h2>

<section id="A4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.1 </span>Text-to-Image Metrics</h3>

<div id="A4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">ImageReward.</span> ImageReward measures the alignment between generated images and human preferences. It is trained on human preference data to predict which image better matches the given text prompt:</p>
<table id="A4.E25" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E25.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{ImageReward}(x,c)=f_{\phi}(x,c)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mtext>ImageReward</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{ImageReward}(x,c)=f_{\phi}(x,c),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(25)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> is the generated image, <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> is the text prompt, and <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> is the reward model trained on human annotations.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">CLIP Score.</span> CLIP Score evaluates the semantic consistency between the generated image and the input text prompt using a pretrained CLIP model:</p>
<table id="A4.E26" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E26.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{CLIPScore}(x,c)=\max(100\cdot\cos(E_{I}(x),E_{T}(c)),0)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mtext>CLIPScore</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>100</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>I</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{CLIPScore}(x,c)=\max(100\cdot\cos(E_{I}(x),E_{T}(c)),0),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(26)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A4.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E_{I}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>I</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E_{I}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E_{T}</annotation></semantics></math> are the image and text encoders of CLIP, and <math id="A4.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\cos(\cdot,\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos(\cdot,\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> denotes cosine similarity.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Aesthetic Score.</span> Aesthetic Score predicts the visual appeal of generated images using a model trained on human aesthetic ratings:</p>
<table id="A4.E27" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E27.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{AestheticScore}(x)=g_{\psi}(E_{I}(x))," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mtext>AestheticScore</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>ψ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>I</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{AestheticScore}(x)=g_{\psi}(E_{I}(x)),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(27)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS1.p3.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A4.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{\psi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>ψ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{\psi}</annotation></semantics></math> is a linear regressor trained on the Aesthetic Visual Analysis (AVA) dataset aesthetic annotations.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.2 </span>Text-to-Video Metrics</h3>

<div id="A4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">VBench.</span> VBench is a comprehensive benchmark that evaluates video generation across multiple dimensions, including subject consistency, background consistency, motion smoothness, aesthetic quality, and imaging quality. The overall score is a weighted combination of these sub-metrics.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">LPIPS.</span> Learned Perceptual Image Patch Similarity measures perceptual similarity between frames:</p>
<table id="A4.E28" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E28.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{LPIPS}(x,y)=\sum_{l}\frac{1}{H_{l}W_{l}}\sum_{h,w}\|w_{l}\odot(\hat{\phi}_{l}^{hw}(x)-\hat{\phi}_{l}^{hw}(y))\|_{2}^{2}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mtext>LPIPS</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mi>l</mi></munder><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>w</mi></mrow></munder><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⊙</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>l</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>w</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>l</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>w</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{LPIPS}(x,y)=\sum_{l}\frac{1}{H_{l}W_{l}}\sum_{h,w}\|w_{l}\odot(\hat{\phi}_{l}^{hw}(x)-\hat{\phi}_{l}^{hw}(y))\|_{2}^{2},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(28)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS2.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A4.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\phi}_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>l</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\phi}_{l}</annotation></semantics></math> are normalized activations from layer <math id="A4.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>l</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l</annotation></semantics></math> of a pretrained network and <math id="A4.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{l}</annotation></semantics></math> are learned weights.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">SSIM.</span> Structural Similarity Index measures the structural similarity between two images:</p>
<table id="A4.E29" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E29.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{SSIM}(x,y)=\frac{(2\mu_{x}\mu_{y}+c_{1})(2\sigma_{xy}+c_{2})}{(\mu_{x}^{2}+\mu_{y}^{2}+c_{1})(\sigma_{x}^{2}+\sigma_{y}^{2}+c_{2})}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mtext>SSIM</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>x</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>y</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>μ</mi><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mi>μ</mi><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{SSIM}(x,y)=\frac{(2\mu_{x}\mu_{y}+c_{1})(2\sigma_{xy}+c_{2})}{(\mu_{x}^{2}+\mu_{y}^{2}+c_{1})(\sigma_{x}^{2}+\sigma_{y}^{2}+c_{2})},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(29)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS2.p3.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A4.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu_{x},\mu_{y}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>x</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>y</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu_{x},\mu_{y}</annotation></semantics></math> are local means, <math id="A4.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{x},\sigma_{y}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>x</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>y</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{x},\sigma_{y}</annotation></semantics></math> are standard deviations, <math id="A4.SS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{xy}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{xy}</annotation></semantics></math> is the covariance, and <math id="A4.SS2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{1},c_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{1},c_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> are stability constants.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">PSNR.</span> Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio measures the reconstruction quality:</p>
<table id="A4.E30" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E30.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{PSNR}(x,y)=10\cdot\log_{10}\left(\frac{\text{R}^{2}}{\text{MSE}(x,y)}\right)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mtext>PSNR</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mrow><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>10</mn></msub><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><msup><mtext>R</mtext><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mtext>MSE</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{PSNR}(x,y)=10\cdot\log_{10}\left(\frac{\text{R}^{2}}{\text{MSE}(x,y)}\right),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(30)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS2.p4.2" class="ltx_p">where R is the maximum possible pixel value, and MSE is the mean squared error.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.3 </span>Class-to-Image Metrics</h3>

<div id="A4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">FID.</span> Fréchet Inception Distance measures the similarity between the distributions of generated and real images:</p>
<table id="A4.E31" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E31.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{FID}=\|\mu_{r}-\mu_{g}\|^{2}+\text{Tr}(\Sigma_{r}+\Sigma_{g}-2(\Sigma_{r}\Sigma_{g})^{1/2})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mtext>FID</mtext><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mrow><mtext>Tr</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{FID}=\|\mu_{r}-\mu_{g}\|^{2}+\text{Tr}(\Sigma_{r}+\Sigma_{g}-2(\Sigma_{r}\Sigma_{g})^{1/2}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(31)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A4.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\mu_{r},\Sigma_{r})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\mu_{r},\Sigma_{r})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\mu_{g},\Sigma_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\mu_{g},\Sigma_{g})</annotation></semantics></math> are the mean and covariance of Inception features for real and generated images.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">sFID.</span> Spatial FID computes FID on spatial feature maps rather than pooled features, better capturing spatial structure.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Inception Score.</span> Inception Score evaluates both quality and diversity of generated samples:</p>
<table id="A4.E32" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E32.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\text{IS}=\exp\left(\mathbb{E}_{x}[D_{KL}(p(y|x)\|p(y))]\right)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>IS</mtext><mo>=</mo><mi>exp</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mi>x</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>L</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{IS}=\exp\left(\mathbb{E}_{x}[D_{KL}(p(y|x)\|p(y))]\right),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(32)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS3.p3.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A4.SS3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(y|x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(y|x)</annotation></semantics></math> is the conditional class distribution from an Inception classifier and <math id="A4.SS3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(y)=\mathbb{E}_{x}[p(y|x)]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mi>x</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(y)=\mathbb{E}_{x}[p(y|x)]</annotation></semantics></math> is the marginal distribution. Higher IS indicates both confident class predictions and diverse class coverage.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>

<section id="A7" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix G </span>Memory Usage Analysis</h2>

<div id="A7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Video generation with DiT models requires substantial GPU memory due to the large spatial-temporal feature maps. We therefore analyze the memory consumption of different acceleration methods on HunyuanVideo across various resolutions and frame settings using a single NVIDIA A800 80GB GPU. As shown in <a href="#A7.T7" title="In Appendix G Memory Usage Analysis ‣ Predict to Skip: Linear Multistep Feature Forecasting for Efficient Diffusion Transformers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>, PrediT introduces minimal memory overhead compared to the original model, with only 1%-2% additional memory usage across all settings. In contrast, prediction-based methods require storing Taylor expansion coefficients and historical gradients, leading to out-of-memory (OOM) errors at most settings. PAB also suffers from OOM at higher resolutions due to its attention caching mechanism. TeaCache shows moderate memory increase but remains functional. These results demonstrate that PrediT achieves significant speedup while maintaining memory efficiency, making it practical for real-world video generation applications.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A7.T7" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 7: </span>Memory Usage (MB) on Different Resolutions and Frames using A800 80GB.</figcaption>
<table id="A7.T7.5" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<thead class="ltx_thead">
<tr id="A7.T7.5.1" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A7.T7.5.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_th_row ltx_border_r ltx_border_tt"><span id="A7.T7.5.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Method</span></th>
<th id="A7.T7.5.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt"><span id="A7.T7.5.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">480p<math id="A7.T7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math>640p<math id="A7.T7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math>45f</span></th>
<th id="A7.T7.5.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt"><span id="A7.T7.5.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">480p<math id="A7.T7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math>640p<math id="A7.T7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math>65f</span></th>
<th id="A7.T7.5.1.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt"><span id="A7.T7.5.1.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">544p<math id="A7.T7.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math>860p<math id="A7.T7.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math>17f</span></th>
<th id="A7.T7.5.1.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt"><span id="A7.T7.5.1.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">544p<math id="A7.T7.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math>860p<math id="A7.T7.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math>65f</span></th>
<th id="A7.T7.5.1.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt"><span id="A7.T7.5.1.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">720p<math id="A7.T7.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math>1280p<math id="A7.T7.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math>129f</span></th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody class="ltx_tbody">

<section id="A8" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix H </span>Supplementary Results for Ablation Studies</h2>

<div id="A8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We conduct more ablation studies on DiT-XL/2 to analyze the impact of different hyperparameter configurations. <a href="#A8.T8" title="In Appendix H Supplementary Results for Ablation Studies ‣ Predict to Skip: Linear Multistep Feature Forecasting for Efficient Diffusion Transformers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> shows results with varying predictor order, dynamics threshold, and correction ratio. Higher-order predictors achieve better quality at the cost of reduced speedup, while smaller <math id="A8.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> values lead to more frequent corrections and improved quality. Notably, with <math id="A8.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}=4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}=4</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A8.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau=0.75" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.75</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau=0.75</annotation></semantics></math>, PrediT achieves FID of 2.17, surpassing the baseline, demonstrating that our method can improve quality while accelerating inference.</p>
</div>

<section id="Ax1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix">Statement on Large Language Model Usage</h2>

<div id="Ax1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In the preparation of this manuscript, Large Language Models (LLMs) were mainly utilized for the purpose of language polishing. The LLM played no role in the generation of core ideas. All final content was thoroughly reviewed and approved by the authors.</p>
</div>
</section>
</article>
